interpretation:
The regulator expects FIs to: (1) report to the FIU when there are reasonable grounds to suspect proceeds of crime; (2) maintain confidentiality of both the report content and the fact of reporting, taking reasonable measures to protect the information from unauthorized access; (3) permit internal sharing of such information within the FI or affiliated group for identification/prevention/reporting purposes despite confidentiality obligations; (4) prohibit tipping off customers that a report has been made, with sanctions for breach; and (5) not allow customer confidentiality or data privacy laws to be used as grounds to refuse statutory reporting.

Element 1 (report to FIU on reasonable grounds of suspicion of proceeds of crime): covered - manual requires reporting suspicious transactions to FIU via GoAML regardless of amount. Element 2 (maintain confidentiality of report/fact of reporting and protect info from unauthorized access): partially covered - manual states SAR information is confidential and treated strictly confidentially, but does not explicitly describe 'reasonable efforts to protect the information from unauthorized access' as a distinct control (e.g., access restrictions, data security measures around SAR records). Element 3 (confidentiality does not restrict internal sharing within FI/affiliated group for identification/prevention/reporting purposes): NOT covered - no language in the excerpts addresses permitted internal information-sharing across the FI or affiliated group notwithstanding confidentiality obligations. Element 4 (prohibition on tipping off customers, with sanctions): covered - extensive tipping-off prohibition and criminal offence language found in the manual. Element 5 (FI may not object to reporting on grounds of customer confidentiality/data privacy): NOT covered - no clause in the excerpts states that customer confidentiality or data privacy considerations cannot be used to refuse or delay statutory reporting.
